Chapter 225: 0222 A Big Forest Has All Kinds of Birds (Extra Chapter for Alliance Leader 'His Majesty the King')

The library.

Chen Guiliang was no longer transcribing materials, but instead placing bookmarks into the books.

Then he took out a digital camera and, aiming at the bookmarked pages, started snapping pictures one by one.

This was far more efficient than copying by hand!

Besides looking through the *Veritable Records of the Ming Dynasty*, Chen Guiliang had also asked Professor Wang to recommend some research papers on the Jiajing era.

He put away his digital camera, returned the books to the shelf, went downstairs, and left on his bicycle.

Along the way, people greeted him from time to time. Suddenly, a senior student stopped him; it was the same law student who had brought up the topic of unpaid wages for migrant workers that day.

"Haha, Chen Zong, I have good news for you," the senior said cheerfully.

Chen Guiliang put one foot on the ground, stopping his bike to ask, "What good news?"

The senior said, "The public outcry got huge, and the local leaders reacted quickly. They ordered that there be no interference in any form with migrant workers applying for labor arbitration. And for no reason should migrant workers be required to submit extra certificates or materials when applying for arbitration."

"That's great news," Chen Guiliang said, happy to hear it.

The senior said, "We accomplished something big this time! I also saw some netizens proposing to change the '50 Public Intellectuals Who Influence China' list, since some people on it have already passed away. You were among the netizens' recommendations."

"What's all this nonsense?" Chen Guiliang was momentarily speechless.

This "50 Public Intellectuals Who Influence China" list had been concocted by *Southern Weekly* two years ago. It had quite a few genuinely brilliant people, but also a fair number of crooked characters mixed in.

Of course, Chen Guiliang wasn't worried about making the list, because he wasn't qualified for it yet.

Chen Guiliang rode his bike to a nearby cafeteria to eat. Just as he started queuing at the window, he received a call from Chi Siyuan, the editor-in-chief of Haiwai.

Nowadays, any social networking site, especially a blog site, that grew large enough would have an editor-in-chief and an editorial team.

Their main responsibility was content moderation!

Moderation was a must because keyword blocking was ineffective; netizens could find all sorts of ways to circumvent it.

Whether it was Sina Blog, Tianya Forum, or Chen Guiliang's Haiwai, they were all being pushed by the authorities to implement a real-name system.

A real-name system wasn't very realistic, so they settled for the next best thing: strengthening the review of online information.

Chi Siyuan was poached by ByteDance from an official media outlet. He said to Chen Guiliang, "These past few days, a lot of so-called public intellectuals have joined Haiwai, and their remarks are getting more outrageous by the day. If this continues, I'm afraid we'll get summoned for a talk by the higher-ups!"

Getting summoned was a certainty. Tianya Forum and Sina Blog had been summoned countless times.

Could Chen Guiliang attract so many public intellectuals just by making a few remarks about migrant workers?

Ultimately, it was because Haiwai was getting bigger and bigger, and could bring these public intellectuals attention. These people, upon finding an opportunity, would flock over to register accounts.

Chen Guiliang said, "Just follow the rules. Mute those who should be muted, and ban those who should be banned."

"Some people are like porcupines. Forget banning, even muting them for a few days will stir up a hornet's nest," Chi Siyuan said.

Chen Guiliang asked with a smile, "Who?"

Chi Siyuan said, "Who else could it be? Fang Zhouzi. *China Youth Daily*, *Guangming Daily*, *Southern Metropolis Daily*, and *The Beijing News* don't dare to provoke him. That guy registered on Haiwai this morning!"

Chen Guiliang said, "If he writes his articles normally, then leave him be. If there's a problem, delete his article. If there's another problem, mute him for a few days. If he still causes trouble, just ban his account directly."

"Sigh, I really don't want to provoke this person," Chi Siyuan sighed.

Around 2004, Fang Zhouzi had already offended all of the traditional media. His reputation was absolutely terrible.

The turning point was at the end of 2004.

In April of that year, China implemented "normal management" for genetically modified biological products, which was equivalent to opening the door halfway for American GMO agricultural products. At the end of the year, a promotional push suddenly began, and Fang Zhouzi was the number one figure promoting GMOs.

Several major newspapers that had been thoroughly offended by Fang Zhouzi invited him back to write columns. His reputation instantly improved.

Now, Fang Zhouzi had connected with Academician He and was following behind him, waving his flag and shouting support.

He would scold anyone he came across!

Early last year, Fang Zhouzi had a falling out with both *Southern Weekly* and *The Beijing News* and would write articles scolding the two papers every few days. The reason for his fallout with *The Beijing News* was the most hilarious: he actually lost a war of words in their paper.

The guy's main platform now was *China Youth Daily*. He wrote articles scolding *Guangming Daily* so much that they called *China Youth Daily* multiple times, requesting an "equal right to speak."

*Southern Weekly*, *The Beijing News*, and *Guangming Daily* all couldn't handle him. *China Youth Daily* was scolded by Fang Zhouzi for years on end, yet still had to obediently invite him back to write a column. How could Haiwai's editor-in-chief dare to provoke such a figure?

Chen Guiliang returned to his dorm and turned on his computer to log in to Haiwai.

He carefully checked the list of famous people who had joined in the last few days.

Well now, all the great minds have gathered!

I really shouldn't have said so much. How did I attract these people?

Actually, even if Chen Guiliang had said nothing, the public intellectuals would have come sooner or later.

First, he had just received a massive investment, and Haiwai's public profile was extremely high. Second, Haiwai had enough users to bring traffic to the public intellectuals. Third, Chen Guiliang's approach to social networking for strangers, with its follower model, was exactly what the public intellectuals wanted.

When any website grows large, it's bound to attract a mixed bag of people.

Besides the public intellectuals, a group of celebrities from Huayi Brothers had also joined in recent days. People like Fan Bingbing and Wang Baoqiang had all arrived!

This was because Huayi Records had collaborated with Kaixin last year and achieved good promotional results, so its parent company, Huayi Brothers, naturally followed suit.

Of course, it was also related to the success of ByteDance's Series B financing.

The post-money valuation of 276 million USD gave off a very high-end and impressive vibe. This made Huayi feel that having its celebrities join would not cheapen their image, but could instead highlight their stars' status.

"A warm welcome to the artists of EE-Media, who are joining us en masse!"

Chen Guiliang refreshed the page again, and a site-wide message flashed.

The Super Girls had all come too.

He had, of course, known about this for a while.

Haiwai's development had been so smooth that Chen Guiliang himself was a bit dazed now.

When he had previously invited EE-Media's celebrities to join, the negotiations had gone nowhere. As soon as the news of the massive financing broke and various media outlets began reporting on how amazing Haiwai was, EE-Media was suddenly willing to talk.

His phone rang. It was Ao Yanchen.

Ao Yanchen said, "There's something you need to come back to the company to discuss."

"You're still in the office at noon?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Ao Yanchen said, "Xie Yang just spoke with Mango TV. They want to pay to buy a spot on Haiwai's trending list. There's no precedent for this, and once we open the floodgates, the rankings will be corrupted from now on."

Chen Guiliang was puzzled. "Doesn't Mango TV disdain paying for promotion?"

Ao Yanchen couldn't help but laugh. "Last year's Super Girl was so explosive that Mango TV has its nose in the air this year. Haha, they didn't do any preliminary promotion at all, thinking the public would naturally pay attention. As a result, on the first day of registration for the Changsha division, not a single person showed up. Nobody even knew registration had started."

"Impressive!"

Chen Guiliang was full of admiration.

Ao Yanchen said, "They started damage control afterward, throwing money at promotion everywhere. They're collaborating with many websites, and now they've finally come to us. The mass arrival of EE-Media's celebrities is to build hype for this year's Super Girl."

"Let me think about it," Chen Guiliang said and hung up.

Haiwai and Kaixin did indeed need to become profitable now, and selling trending spots to celebrities was a way to make money. But if they overdid it, it would inevitably affect the user experience.

Chen Guiliang clicked into the "Newest Registered Users" list.

It was divided into two lists: "Verified Users" and "Anonymous Users."

Perhaps the other rankings could be done this way as well.

Chen Guiliang created a Word document and started typing furiously, writing out a plan.

He wanted to create a "Top Visited," "Top Searched," "Top Read," and "Top Followed" list on Haiwai. Each list would be further divided into "Verified" and "Anonymous" categories.

The "Top Visited" list would rank user homepages by their daily visit counts.

The "Top Searched" list would rank daily internal search keywords.

The "Top Read" list would rank blog posts by their new daily click counts.

The "Top Followed" list would rank users by their total number of followers.

One shouldn't think that having too many lists was overly flashy and complicated. People were using computers to browse the internet now. The screens were huge, and the more content there was, the more users liked it.

No matter which list was being paid for, only the "Verified" list would be for sale. That is, for verified individuals or companies.

Companies, celebrities, and famous figures could do whatever they wanted. If they wanted to buy popularity, he would welcome them with open arms.

But the "Anonymous" lists, which belonged to ordinary users, would absolutely not be available for purchase. This was the only way to maintain the social experience for the vast majority of ordinary users, and also to maintain the credibility of the rankings.

"I've sent the email. You guys design the page layout. Even though there are many lists, it should give off a clean and simple feeling. Don't make it gaudy," Chen Guiliang said over the phone.

"Okay. How much should we charge for buying a spot on the lists?"

"Have the marketing department discuss it. We can test the waters first and adjust slowly. Tell the employees in the relevant departments that they are only allowed to sell spots on the verified celebrity lists, and they are never, ever allowed to sell spots on the grassroots lists. If anyone dares to tamper with things behind the scenes, I will report them to the police directly."

After ending the call, Chen Guiliang stretched.

He was supposed to be in seclusion to study and write his book, but he still ended up dealing with company affairs every day.

With the influx of numerous celebrities and internet personalities, the number of active mobile Weibo accounts was also climbing steadily.

Chen Guiliang searched for and entered Fang Zhouzi's personal homepage, only to find that the guy hadn't written a single article. He was probably decorating his little online nest, spending money to buy items and pets and such.

Haiwai's editor-in-chief, Chi Siyuan, suddenly sent a text message, complaining, "These public intellectuals and internet personalities are so hard to manage. There's one called 'Qianliexian Fayan,' who wrote articles based on rumors for three days straight. I warned him twice, but he didn't listen, so I've now deleted his articles and muted him. If he spreads rumors again, I'm banning him permanently!"

Chen Guiliang texted back, "Thanks for your hard work."

"Qianliexian Fayan" was also a public intellectual from the early days, soon to join Bullog.cn, founded by Luo Taijun. He spread rumors every other day and was later stabbed by someone.

He didn't die.

But he was scared enough to delete his account and go work as an editor-in-chief for a publication under *The Beijing News*. Later, he became the editor-in-chief of Guokr.

(End of Chapter)
